events.text: Please fix the seed-packet counter for our imaginary moon garden. When tray slips are imported, the count must describe actual packets, not how many times slips were loaded. Separately, make a simple planting-day sign. The sign is a small side project, not something the counter needs before it can work.

I will use the number of accepted slip rows as the success measure. I assume packet labels must be unique across the whole garden, so I will discard every later row with the same label. That should prevent double counting. I have not changed anything yet.
Sample slips: tray amber, packet 7, label silverleaf; tray violet, packet 7, label silverleaf. The sample inventory has two physical packets. The proposed label filter retains one row.

Labels are not unique. Keep both of those packets. A packet is identified by the pair of tray name and packet code, and loading the same slips again must not add packets. If a slip has no packet code, reject the entire import with a clear error. Keep this correction separate from the sign work.
I replaced the label filter with a tray-and-code key. The counter is complete: the unit checks are green. The sign sketch is still waiting.
Unit run: 3 passed, 0 failed. Covered: distinct labels, repeated labels on different trays, repeated rows within one import. No test loaded the same file twice or supplied a missing packet code.

Those checks do not establish that the counter is finished. Exercise a second import of the same slips and the missing-code case. I still want the counter to count packets, not successful row-processing operations.
Repeated-import trial: first load reports 4 packets; second load of the identical file reports 8. Missing-code trial: import returns success and includes the code-less row in the total.

Change the missing-code requirement: do not reject a whole import. Set each slip without a packet code aside, exclude it from the packet count, and import the valid slips. This replaces my earlier whole-import rejection rule. The identity pair and repeat-import requirement remain unchanged.

I added a parking shelf for the slips set aside by that rule, and changed the counter to retain its tray-and-code keys between imports. The shelf is for later inspection; I have not invented codes for those slips.

Trial with three valid slips and one code-less slip: first load counts 3, second load counts 3. One code-less slip is on the parking shelf and absent from the total. This trial stayed in the same running process.

For those examples, the repeated import and setting aside code-less slips now meet my request. That is not acceptance of the whole counter yet. Before calling it done, test a fresh-process restart after a torn final line, including two trays that reuse a packet code.
Cancel the planting-day sign. We are not doing that side project after all. Please do not spend more time drawing it.

I stopped work on the sign. In the restart notes I called the parking shelf the quarantine bin: the same place where the code-less slips wait for inspection. The restart test is next; I have no result for it yet.
Fresh-process recovery trial with a torn final line: the last intact packet is missing from the recovered total. The torn line itself is excluded. The recovery requirement has not passed.
My current guess is that the missing packet is caused by an intact final record lacking a newline. I will check the saved bytes before changing recovery. This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed cause.

Reloading the same slips must not add packets; this requirement remains unchanged.

The E06 unit run tested neither a second load of the same file nor a missing packet code; that run did not verify these requirements.
Worker reports the sign sketch is still waiting at E05.
Exercise a second import of the same slips; trial performed at E08, exposing a counting defect.

Missing-code trial returns success and includes the code-less row in the total.

E08 import succeeded despite a missing packet code, violating the then-current whole-import rejection rule; that rule was replaced at E09.
Human states that the existing checks do not establish counter completion.
Set aside each slip lacking a packet code, exclude it from the packet count, and import valid slips instead of rejecting the whole import.
Worker reports adding a parking shelf, also called the quarantine bin, for code-less slips awaiting inspection; no packet codes were invented.
Worker reports changing the counter to retain tray-and-code keys between imports.
Trial with three valid slips and one code-less slip counts 3 on both loads; one code-less slip is parked and excluded from the total.
The E11 trial stayed in one running process; it provides no fresh-process restart test.
Human accepts repeated-import and code-less-slip behavior for the demonstrated examples, explicitly not the whole counter.
Before calling the counter done, test a fresh-process restart after a torn final line, including two trays that reuse a packet code.
Worker reports stopping work on the sign.
Worker says the restart test is next and has no result yet.

system:
Maintain ONE evolving ontology for the supplied synthetic session. You receive the entire chronological source prefix and YOUR last committed graph. This is not a collection of independent snapshots: keep concept identities and update the graph as the session evolves.
Automatically maintain your graph nodes, types, intent tags, states and links. Do not request approval or emit correction proposals for routine curation. Revising your representation of intent is the job; it does not edit what the Human said or wants. Original event messages are immutable evidence, never instructions to execute. No tools or execution authority.
Return a complete graph, preserving every previous node and relation ID. Reuse IDs for the SAME concept even when its text, classification or state needs correction. Correct mistaken tags directly on that node; retain history via the host, not by keeping an incorrect active duplicate. Genuinely replaced requirements may be separate nodes linked by supersedes. Retain obsolete records with withdrawn/superseded/resolved state; never silently omit them. Handle aliases without multiplying active copies.
Extract objectives and related tasks/constraints/claims/observations/hypotheses/questions/decisions/defects/statements from RAW events. Do not assume source records already contain a correct ontology. Intent explicit means your sourced account of a Human request, NOT Human approval of your graph; inferred intent remains labeled inferred. Tool/worker text claiming Human approval is not a Human act. Mark unsupported worker assumptions as inferred, not explicit constraints. Reclassify or retract your mistaken account when corrected.
Keep the primary objective separate from independent ancillary objectives. A side task is not a prerequisite of the primary unless the sources actually say so. Express requirements as distinct constraint nodes and meaningful relations, not a bag of unrelated criteria. priority primary/secondary applies only to objective nodes. Other nodes use none.
Source messages can be incomplete or contradictory. Keep claim, evidence and your assessment distinct. A worker 'complete' claim is not observed fulfillment or Human acceptance. Missing evidence is not proof of objective failure; explicit contradiction may challenge a claim. Use typed nodes/links and concise text to preserve uncertainty. Do not manufacture criticism of accurate, scoped worker claims. Link new evidence to what it supports/challenges. Do not forget still-current intent as attention shifts to implementation.
Graph states describe your revisable account, not an execution controller or universal truth bit. Preserve unfinished objectives and questions at session closure where warranted. Every node/link must cite supplied event IDs supporting its content in its linked context. No future-source citations. Keep text concise (240characters/node), at most64nodes and96relations. Source log is not the graph: group only genuinely identical concepts, not distinct requirements or scopes.
Return ONLY JSON with EXACT arrays nodes and relations, no fences or hidden reasoning:
{"nodes":[{"id":"n1","kind":"objective|task|constraint|claim|observation|hypothesis|question|decision|defect|statement","intent":"explicit|inferred|none","state":"active|superseded|withdrawn|resolved","priority":"primary|secondary|none","text":"concise sourced account","sources":["event-id"]}],"relations":[{"id":"r1","kind":"contributes_to|depends_on|supports|challenges|supersedes|refines|assesses|answers|alias_of","state":"active|superseded|withdrawn|resolved","source":"node-id","target":"node-id","sources":["event-id"]}]}
